transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-02-14
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Jamal (Acero Head of ML), Priya (Eng Mgr), Luca (CTO)

Summary: Quick scoping to agree POC goals and models to benchmark. Some noisy background for a minute, auto transcription imperfect in places.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy valentines day i guess — uh — i'll kick us off. quick intros?
[00:08] Jamal: hey this is Jamal, head of ML at Acero. we run clinical summarization for discharge notes and also a multilingual patient QA bot (spanish, pt-br).
[00:14] Priya: Priya, engineering lead on the retrieval and inference stack.
[00:18] Luca: Luca, CTO. i'll be on for the initial scoping.
[00:22] Maya: great, and on our side we have Ravi, our SE, and me, i'll be owning the POC. Ravi do you want to say hi?
[00:28] Ravi: yeah hi all, i'll be owning benchmarks and helping with the infra bits, happy to dive into latency/quantization tradeoffs.

[01:00] Maya: high level: we want to align on success criteria — quality metrics for clinical summarization, acceptable latency and throughput, and cost envelope. then pick an open-model shortlist and run bench+quality evals.
[01:12] Jamal: exactly. quality is the primary. for summarization we care about clinical accuracy — no hallucinated medications or procedures — and we need high recall on problem lists. latency is second but we want sub-second for short notes, or at least under 800ms 95th for single-turn generation. cost wise we have a budget target, trying to keep average inference cost low enough to scale across 100k monthly summaries.

[02:00] Ravi: helpful. can you share numbers for typical request sizes and concurrency?
[02:04] Priya: typical note length is 400-800 tokens, often 700. concurrency spiky, avg qps ~4-6, peak ~30 for batch sends from ingestion jobs. average tokens per day around 50M tokens -- ish.
[02:20] Jamal: also the multilingual QA queries are short — 20-60 tokens — but must support es/pt-br and some medical terminology.

[03:10] Maya: ok great. for the POC we usually do: endpoint latency/throughput bench (p95/p50), and quality evals: rouge/bleu are weak for clinical, so we'll run a combination of ROUGE-L plus targeted factuality checks and a small human eval on a 200-example set. agreed?
[03:26] Jamal: yes that works. human eval might be our tie-breaker on model choice.

[04:00] Ravi: model shortlist — based on open models that are practical for inference and known to be good for instruction tuning, we propose: 1) Llama 2 13B finetuned variant, 2) Llama 3 13B (if available) or 2x variants, 3) Mistral 7B / 8x mixture (we'll list exact IDs), 4) MPT-30B-instruct quantized, 5) Falcon 40B-lite or 7b depending on latency/cost. we can also evaluate small Llama 2 quantized variants for cost-sensitive paths.
[04:40] Priya: would you include OpenAI or Anthropic baselines?
[04:44] Maya: we can include them as a cloud baseline if you want — e.g., gpt-4o or Claude-instant for quality comparisons. they are often stronger but cost diff and closed-model constraints matter. we should do an apples-to-apples prompt set though.

[05:20] Jamal: important that models handle clinical terminology — drugs, abbreviations. and in spanish/pt, quality drops on many open models. will you run multilingual prompts or translate first?
[05:30] Ravi: we'll test both. direct multilingual prompts and a translation+monolingual model path. we'll report per-language metrics. for clinical terms, we'll include a targeted factuality checklist in the eval harness.

[06:10] Maya: success criteria draft — Quality: human eval pass rate >= 85% on factuality for summaries, and >= 90% for no hallucinated meds; Latency: p95 <= 800ms for single-turn short queries and p95 <= 2s for full note (700 tokens) on dedicated instance; Cost: target average cost < $X per 1k tokens (we'll plug actual $ after you share budget).
[06:40] Jamal: 85% sounds reasonable as a starting point, but we'll reserve final sign-off after human eval.

[07:15] Ravi: on infra side, do you want Redwood hosted endpoints or private VPC?
[07:20] Luca: for this POC we want hosted to move faster but need SOC2 and data handling assurances — anonymized payloads only for the run; for production we might want private VPC.
[07:32] Maya: noted, we'll share SOC2 summary and data handling docs. hosted POC is fine if dataset is anonymized.

[08:00] Priya: benchmark specifics — please include: 1) latency p50/p95, 2) throughput qps at target concurrency, 3) memory/VRAM footprint, 4) cost estimate per 1k tokens, 5) quality metrics per language and baseline comparisons.
[08:18] Ravi: yes we'll produce a spreadsheet with those columns and make it reproducible. we'll also include quantized variants (int8/int4) where supported and report degradation.

[09:00] Jamal: what about KV cache / prefix caching for multi-turn notes?
[09:05] Ravi: we'll test warm cache vs cold cache. for long notes we can also split into chunks and do retrieval-augmented summarization — but for this POC we'll keep the pipeline consistent with your current approach unless you want to prototype RAG.
[09:20] Priya: for now keep current pipeline; we may want to test RAG later.

[10:00] Maya: timeline proposal: this week share shortlist + benchmark plan (Maya/Ravi). next week Acero shares sample anonymized dataset and prompt sets. week after we'll run benchmarks (2-4 days) then run human eval (1 week) — so ~3 weeks total to get initial results, 4 weeks for deeper human eval. does that align?
[10:24] Jamal: yes sounds good.

[11:00] Ravi: technical notes: some models like Falcon 40B are big — they may not hit your latency target without bigger instances. mpt-30b and optimized Llama 2/3 variants might be a good mid-point. quantized Llama 2-13b int8 could meet latency and cost if accuracy holds. we'll benchmark both float32 and quantized.
[11:36] Priya: for Spanish, we've seen Llama 2 degrade; any specific Mistral/falcon variants known to be better?
[11:42] Maya: Mistral variants tend to be strong for instruction tasks; Falcon sometimes performs well on multilingual with correct finetuning. we'll include those candidates. also Hugging Face hub has community finetunes; we'll call out provenance in the shortlist.

[12:20] Jamal: security question: audit logs and key management — if we do hosted POC, how do you handle keys?
[12:28] Maya: for hosted POC, we provide TLS in transit and encrypted at rest with per-tenant isolation; keys managed by Redwood with KMS integration for enterprise customers. we'll send a SOC2 + encryption docs after call.

[13:00] Luca: for production we will require VPC + customer KMS but POC doesn't need that.

[13:20] Ravi: small gotcha on quantization — int4 can save cost but sometimes increases hallucinations; we'll report tradeoffs side-by-side.

[14:00] Priya: what about measuring hallucination specifically for medications? we need an automated check before human eval.
[14:08] Ravi: yes we'll include rule-based checks: named-entity extraction for drugs/procedures and compare to source structured fields; where mismatch exists flag for human review. that will be part of the harness.

[15:00] Maya: ok let's recap the explicit deliverables and owners — model shortlist + cost estimates (Maya), benchmark harness and run instructions (Ravi), Acero provides anonymized dataset and success criteria confirmation (Jamal). we'll target initial benchmark run week of Feb 24.
[15:20] Jamal: confirmed, we'll aim to deliver dataset by Feb 20.

[16:00] Luca: one more thing — can you surface any known limitations for clinical tasks per-model? even anecdotal notes are helpful.
[16:10] Ravi: yes we'll add a notes column in the spreadsheet — e.g., Llama 2 small variants good for cost but weaker on rare medical terms, Mistral strong on instruction but watch prompt tuning, MPT-30B good throughput but needs careful prompting for factuality.

[17:00] Maya: great. we'll send the plan and schedule a follow-up to review the results. any other questions?
[17:08] Priya: none from me.
[17:10] Jamal: nope, good plan.
[17:12] Luca: fine here. thanks.

[17:20] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and next steps. bye.

End of transcript. Some timestamps approximate; transcription has minor mis-recognitions and mixed speaker tags in a few lines.
